declarations.checkedType: agent(channel: string, deliver_to: agent(value: message) -> null with E3) -> never with credential | throw[api_error | auth_error] | E3 | io
declarations.documentation:
Serve a channel forever, delivering each incoming message to @deliver_to@ as one `message` value;
shaped like `time.watch` so it composes under `parallel [ … ]`. Bot posts (this bot's own replies
included) are not delivered, so replying from @deliver_to@ cannot loop. Raises `discord_error` when the
gateway will not open — opening it is this call's job, so an invalid token stops the watch as
`auth_error` rather than failing the provider.

Delivery is exactly once within one live gateway connection and guaranteed neither way across a
reconnect or a runtime restart: the gateway has no per-event acknowledgement and Discord backfills
nothing onto a fresh session, so a message can be missed, far more rarely repeated, and nothing here
dedups. A bot that must miss nothing keeps the `id` of the last message it handled somewhere durable
and closes the gap with `list_messages`.

@author@ is an enumerable snowflake, so pass it through `crypto.pseudonym` before letting it leave the
program. @display_name@ beside it is self-chosen and not unique: address with it, authorize on @author@.
declarations.name: watch_messages

parameters.label: channel

parameters.label: deliver_to

The channel's messages posted after @after@, in posted order — the reconciliation `watch_messages`
needs across a reconnect. @after@ is a message id, not a timestamp: keep the `id` of the last message
you handled durably and hand it back here; an empty @after@ reads the newest @limit@ instead.

The answer is the same `message` value the watch delivers, attachments downloaded and this bot's own
posts dropped — a page of image-heavy history pays for every attachment on it, so keep @limit@ to what
you will actually process. @limit@ is clamped into Discord's 1-100, so a wide gap takes several reads and an empty
page, not a short one, marks it closed. Nothing dedups. Raises `discord_error` as `send_message` does.

declarations.documentation:
A form: a button that opens a dialog of @fields@, and submitting the dialog is the answer
(`submitted`), carrying every field's text. Two steps because that is Discord's physics — text input
exists only inside a dialog — so a form renders as one button reading @label@ above a dialog titled
@title@. Opening the dialog and closing it again is not an answer: the question stays open and any
control can still answer it. Discord takes 1 to 5 fields.

declarations.documentation:
Post @prompt@ with @controls@ as one message and block until someone in the channel completes one of
them, returning which control answered and with what. Any member of the channel may answer and the
first completed interaction is the answer; opening a form's dialog completes nothing.

Once answered — or ended without an answer, which leaves `(expired)` — the controls are stripped off the
message and the outcome left in their place, best effort either way. That record reads as the control's
own text (a `button`'s or `form`'s @label@, a `select`'s picked @option@) and names the answerer as a
mention, while the @by@ the `answer` carries is the raw id.

`ask` holds no time limit: a deadline is `time.with_deadline` around it, a withdrawal is
`region.cancel_by_id` on the fiber holding it. A runtime restart interrupts the wait under the
at-most-once rule (a catchable panic) and leaves the posted controls stale, so a late click gets
Discord's own "interaction failed" notice; ask again. Raises `discord_error` when opening the gateway
(an invalid token is `auth_error`), posting the question, or opening a dialog fails.

A control past one of Discord's caps splits two ways: presentation is clamped (a @label@ or @title@ is
shortened, a blank one renders as the control's @id@), while an @id@, a `select` option, a `field`
@value@ and a count past `limits` fail the ask as `api_error`. `check_controls` answers all of that
purely, where the controls are built.

@by@ on the answer is an enumerable snowflake, so pass it through `crypto.pseudonym` before letting it
leave the program. The @display_name@ beside it is self-chosen and not unique: an answer that depends on
who gave it must read @by@.
declarations.name: ask

parameters.documentation: The channel to ask in — its membership is who may answer.
parameters.label: channel

parameters.documentation: The question posted above the controls.
parameters.label: prompt

parameters.documentation: What the human may complete: `button` / `select` / `form` values, rendered in order. Each control's @id@ must be distinct within one ask — the id is the correlation key Discord carries back, so a repeat is unroutable rather than merely untidy (the sidecar keeps the first and warns). Discord fits at most 5 rows on a message: up to 5 buttons share a row, each dropdown takes one of its own.
parameters.label: controls

declarations.documentation:
Discord's limits on what one question may present, as data. Lengths are in characters; the renderer
counts UTF-16 code units and Katari's `string.length` counts code points, so the two disagree by one per
astral character — shorten anything sitting within a couple of characters of its cap rather than
trusting either count. Each field says what happens past it: a presentation string is clamped, a
load-bearing one is fatal.
declarations.name: caps

parameters.documentation: One message's text: at most this many characters, fatal past it. It caps an `ask`'s @prompt@ and `send_message` / `try_send`'s @text@, and it is the one number here that no control carries — so `check_controls` cannot see it, and a caller building a prompt out of text it did not write must bound that text itself against this.
parameters.label: message_text

parameters.documentation: A `button`'s @label@ — and a `form`'s opening button's: at most this many characters, clamped past it.
parameters.label: button_label

parameters.documentation: A `select`'s @label@, the placeholder line: at most this many characters, clamped past it. Blank is legal here alone — it leaves Discord's own default line.
parameters.label: select_label

parameters.documentation: Each of a `select`'s @options@: 1 to this many characters, fatal outside it — the option's text is the answer.
parameters.label: select_option

parameters.documentation: How many @options@ one `select` may offer: 1 to this many, fatal outside it.
parameters.label: select_options

parameters.documentation: A `form`'s @title@: at most this many characters, clamped past it. Discord's own number — the twin contract asks for 24, which is a convention rather than a cap (see `form`'s @title@).
parameters.label: form_title

parameters.documentation: How many `field` boxes one `form`'s dialog may hold: 1 to this many, fatal outside it.
parameters.label: form_fields

parameters.documentation: A `field`'s @label@: at most this many characters, clamped past it.
parameters.label: field_label

parameters.documentation: A `field`'s @value@, the prefilled draft: at most this many characters, fatal past it — a submit approves exactly these values. Blank is legal: it is the absence of a prefill.
parameters.label: field_value

parameters.documentation: A `button`'s, `select`'s or `field`'s @id@: 1 to this many characters, fatal outside it — it is the routing key, never presentation.
parameters.label: control_id

parameters.documentation: A `form`'s @id@: 1 to this many characters, fatal outside it. Shorter than @control_id@ because the form's dialog carries a prefix on the same identifier.
parameters.label: form_id

parameters.documentation: How many rows of controls one message may carry, fatal past it.

declarations.name: control_check
declarations.signature: type control_check = valid | invalid

declarations.documentation:
Check @controls@ against Discord's caps locally and answer with a value — `valid`, or `invalid`
carrying one sentence naming the offending control. Pure: no credential, no io, nothing to catch, so it
belongs where the controls are built rather than where they are asked, and it is deliberately not wired
into `ask`.

What it reports is wider than what `ask` fails on, on purpose:

- Fatal, as `ask` would be: a blank or over-long @id@, a blank or over-long `select` option, a count
  outside `limits`' @select_options@ / @form_fields@ / @rows@, an over-long `field` @value@, and an
  empty @controls@ (a question nobody can answer, which Discord posts happily).
- Silent, which `ask` survives and a program still wants to know: a label, placeholder or title past
  its cap is shortened, and a blank one renders as the control's own @id@ — so the channel's lasting
  record of what was decided reads as an internal key, or as most of a sentence.
- Duplicate ids, which nothing else catches at all: Discord returns the id and nothing more, so the
  sidecar keeps the first and pressing the second control completes the first control's answer. A
  `form`'s @fields@ are checked the same way, since `submitted.values` is keyed by field id.

Lengths are counted in code points while the renderer counts UTF-16 units, so an astral character is
one here and two there.
declarations.name: check_controls

parameters.documentation: The controls one `ask` would present, in the order it would render them.
parameters.label: controls

controls.description: The controls one `ask` would present, in the order it would render them.

anyOf.description:
button: A clickable button: pressing it is the answer (`clicked`), with no second step. @id@ returns
verbatim, so a program branches on the id it wrote rather than on the label a human reads.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

id.description: The answer's identity; returned verbatim as `clicked.id`. At most 100 characters and never shortened — it is how Discord routes the press back, so an over-long or blank one fails the ask as `api_error`.

label.description: What the button reads on screen; at most 80 characters, shortened with `…` beyond that, and rendered as @id@ when blank.

anyOf.description:
form: A form: a button that opens a dialog of @fields@, and submitting the dialog is the answer
(`submitted`), carrying every field's text. Two steps because that is Discord's physics — text input
exists only inside a dialog — so a form renders as one button reading @label@ above a dialog titled
@title@. Opening the dialog and closing it again is not an answer: the question stays open and any
control can still answer it. Discord takes 1 to 5 fields.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

fields.description: The boxes the dialog presents, in order.

items.description:
field: One text box of a `form`: labelled, optionally prefilled, optionally multi-line. A prefilled box is
how a draft gets edited — the human submits the program's proposal changed or unchanged, so the program
never has to guess which parts were accepted.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

id.description: The key this box's text lands under in `submitted.values`. At most 100 characters and never shortened, so an over-long or blank one fails the ask as `api_error`.

label.description: What the box is labelled on screen; at most 45 characters, shortened with `…` beyond that, and rendered as @id@ when blank.

multiline.description: Whether the box is a multi-line paragraph rather than one line; defaults to one line.

value.description: The text the box starts with — a draft to edit; defaults to empty. At most 4000 characters and never shortened, since a submit approves exactly these values: an over-long one fails the ask as `api_error`, for the program to shorten deliberately.

id.description: The answer's identity; returned verbatim as `submitted.id`. At most 94 characters — six shorter than any other id, because the dialog's own identifier carries a prefix — and never shortened; an over-long or blank one fails the ask as `api_error` where the question posts.

label.description: What the opening button reads on screen; at most 80 characters, shortened with `…` beyond that, and rendered as @id@ when blank.

title.description: The dialog's title; keep it to 24 characters, which is the twin contract's bound rather than Discord's own 45, so a form written here also renders on the Slack twin. Past 45 it is shortened with `…`, and a blank title renders as @id@.

anyOf.description:
select: A dropdown: picking one option is the answer (`chose`), carrying the option's own text. Reach for it
when the options are data the program computed; a fixed set of choices is clearer as one `button` each,
because then every branch has an id the program named. Discord takes at most 25 options of 100
characters.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

id.description: The answer's identity; returned verbatim as `chose.id`. At most 100 characters and never shortened — see `button`'s @id@.

label.description: The placeholder line shown while nothing is picked; at most 150 characters, shortened with `…` beyond that. Blank leaves Discord's own default line in place.

options.description: The options offered; the picked one returns as `chose.option`. Each is 1 to 100 characters and is never shortened, since the option's own text is the answer: an over-long or blank one fails the ask as `api_error`.

and what in one line — the first problem found, in declaration order, so a fix at a time converges.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

reason.description: Which control, and what is wrong with it.

distinct, and nothing would be shortened or substituted on the way to the channel.
